items.title: 18.7.3 Effect of Ligand Exchange on the Colour of Complexes

source_refs.note: Topic 18.7.3 with Table 18.4 and Quick Check 18.5, answered (PDF 29-30). Answers were derived and need review.

blocks.text: Exchanging ligands changes the size of the d orbital splitting, delta E, for the metal ion. The frequency of the light absorbed therefore changes, and so does the colour seen. In each case the new ligands (NH3 or Cl-) form a more stable complex than the original H2O ligands, with a different delta E and so a different colour.

blocks.caption: Ligand exchange and colour change (book's Table 18.4)

blocks.prompt: Write the equation for [Cu(H2O)4(OH)2](s) dissolving in excess ammonia.
Pink [Co(H2O)6]2+ turns blue with conc. HCl. Explain the change using d orbital splitting.
blocks.explanation: Four Cl- replace six H2O and the octahedral ion becomes tetrahedral [CoCl4]2-. Cl- causes less splitting than H2O and tetrahedral splitting is smaller anyway, so delta E falls; the complex absorbs lower-energy (red/orange) light and so looks blue.

blocks.prompt: For [Co(H2O)6]2+ + 4Cl- -> [CoCl4]2- + 6H2O, give the coordination number and shape of the product.

items: New ligands change delta E, so the absorbed frequency and the colour change.
